items.t: Optispark distributor misfires, stalls or won't start
items.job: Replace Optispark distributor (cap, rotor and housing)
items.note: Parts: an aftermarket TRQ distributor for 1994-1996 Caprices lists at about $99 at 1A Auto; one owner paid about $748 for a dealer unit. Labor: no published book time was found. Owners' dealer bills for 1994-1996 police Caprices ran about $1,300-$1,600 for Optispark plus water pump, which works out to roughly 3-5 hours. Replace a leaking water pump at the same time. If only the cap and rotor are bad, GM's bulletin allows a cheaper service kit.

items.t: Water pump leaks coolant and the engine overheats
items.job: Replace water pump and refill coolant
items.note: Parts and labor from Go-Parts' 1992-1997 Caprice water pump guide: aftermarket pumps about $53-$100, ACDelco about $80-$160, shop labor about $200-$350. RepairPal cross-check: $896-$1,209 total. Cost rises a lot if coolant ruined the Optispark or the engine overheated.

items.t: Oil leak from the front engine seals
items.job: Replace front cover and water pump drive seals
items.note: From an owner thread on a 1996 LT1: online quotes were about $350-$800 labor plus parts, and a water pump, cap and rotor bought at the same time came to under $200. The balancer seal alone is a much smaller job.

items.t: Front lower ball joint nuts may loosen (recall)
items.job: Recall 96V-018 ball joint nut inspection and repair
items.note: Free at a Chevrolet dealer if not already done. Check the VIN.

items.t: Wheel lug nuts may not be tight (recall)
items.note: Free at a Chevrolet dealer if not already done. Check the VIN.

items.t: Rear lower control arms can crack on police and taxi cars (recall)
items.job: Recall 96V-020 rear lower control arm replacement
items.note: Free at a Chevrolet dealer for covered police and taxi package cars. Check the VIN.

items.t: Fuel pump fails and the engine stalls
items.note: No parts-retailer price could be fetched, so this is based on YourMechanic's Caprice fuel pump estimates: $566-$655 total for 1990-1993 B-body Caprices, with labor averaging about $343. Adding the sending unit costs more.

items.t: Door window won't go up or sits crooked
items.job: Replace window regulator or motor (if new rollers don't fix it)
items.note: Based on RepairPal's 1991-1996 Caprice window regulator/motor estimate of $283-$503 total. Replacing just the worn rollers costs much less; GM and Dorman rollers are cheap.

items.t: Serpentine belt chirps or power steering cuts out
items.note: YourMechanic: Caprice idler pulley about $151 average ($27 parts, $123 labor), $178-$204 for 1989-1993 5.7L cars. The belt price is extra and was not sourced separately.

items.t: Worn ball joints and fast front tire wear
items.job: Replace front lower control arm with ball joint (one side)
items.note: YourMechanic: 1996 Caprice front lower control arm about $549 (shop/dealer $653-$957); average parts about $96. An alignment afterward is extra.
